title: cbatch-misconfig-lab-notes
body:
One-off lab scratchpad for the intermittent throughput regression we saw on prod/stage (observed 2024-11-01 -> spike 2024-11-03 AM). Goal: capture commands tried, raw error/log snippets, hypotheses, and quick experiments so we can hand this to SRE/owner later. Keep notes terse; rough chronology + micro-hypotheses.

Incident summary:
- Symptom: ~20-35% drop in tokens/sec for short-chat workloads (seq_len ~64) on node pool `dedicated-pool-a` starting 2024-11-01 03:00 UTC. No concurrent scaling events recorded in autoscaler logs for that pool.
- Affected: routes using continuous-batcher config `cbatch-v2-low-latency` and model variants with small batch-optimized kernels.
- Not affected: long-seq workloads, purely embedding routes.

Quick metrics snapshot (from query to metrics DB):
- baseline (2024-10-28 00:00 -> 2024-10-30): median throughput: 8200 tok/s per GPU, p50 latency 38ms
- regression window (2024-11-01 03:00 -> 2024-11-03 08:00): median throughput: 5200 tok/s per GPU, p50 latency 46ms, tail latencies spiking
- CPU & GPU util: GPU util steady, CPU for batching thread pool spiked to 70-80% intermittently

Initial commands / checks performed:
- pulled recent batcher config on a few nodes: `rictl node-config get --node=dedicated-1 --component=batcher --format yaml` -> confirmed `target_window_ms: 6` and `min_window_ms: 2` for cbatch-v2
- inspected runtime flags: `ps aux | grep runtime | grep batch` -> unchanged between healthy and degraded nodes
- snapshot of in-memory batch occupancy counters via debug endpoint: `curl -s http://localhost:17000/debug/batcher/occupancy` -> saw frequent small batches (1-3 requests) even at high queue depth
- checked request routing logs: `grep "route=chat-small" /var/log/proxy-requests.log | tail -n 500` -> a subset of requests were marked `route_hint=sticky-region:eu-west` with additional header `x-traffic-split=canary`

Representative log snippets (sanitized):
- "batcher: window closed early: occupancy 2 < expected 6, reason=timer_expired, node_clock_skew=7ms"
- "prefill: kv-cache-hit, but cache-key-mismatch detected, invalidating prefix (len=16)"
- "autoscale: pool target unchanged, but active_slots_changed from 128 -> 96 (rebalance)"
- "route-matcher: override applied, client-sticky -> route variant fallback=cpu-quantized"

Commands and small experiments (results inline):
1) force larger window for the batcher on a single canary node:
   - cmd: `rictl batcher set --node=dedicated-canary-3 --name=cbatch-v2-low-latency --target_window_ms=15`
   - result: per-node throughput increased ~18% for the canary after ~2 minutes. p50 latency increased moderately.
2) disable per-request sticky routing at proxy level for 10m:
   - cmd: `proxyctl feature-toggle sticky-routing off --route chat-small`
   - result: traffic rebalanced across more nodes; aggregate throughput recovered ~10% but some tails persisted.
3) evict shard rebalancer on a test node to prevent slot compaction:
   - cmd: `systemctl stop shard-rebalancer` then monitor occupancy
   - result: batch occupancy on that node smoothed (fewer 1-3 sized batches), throughput improved ~12% locally.
4) rolled back last kernel-selection change on 2 nodes (PR #812)
   - result: no measurable improvement compared to canary-window-change above.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): batching window getting shortened in practice because of interaction between per-route sticky routing and rebalance events -> many requests get funneled into a small number of slots, causing fragmented occupancy and early timer expirations. Evidence: logs showing `window closed early` + occupancy counters showing many small batches and rebalance logs showing active_slots shrink. Can reproduce partially by toggling sticky-routing.
- H2: KV-prefill invalidations increase per-request overhead and cause longer time-to-fill windows (so queue doesn't fill). Evidence: cache-key-mismatch logs and some increase in CPU cycles for prefill threads. But this doesn't fully explain small-batch frequency.
- H3: A subtle autoscaler rebalance bug reduces available batching slots during low-latency mode (we saw active_slots drop from 128->96) which increases fragmentation. Evidence: autoscale logs. Harder to reproduce in lab without running autoscaler.
- H4 (low): recent kernel selection PR (#812) degraded throughput for small-batch path. Evidence weak: rollback didn't help.

Interim conclusions:
- The biggest lever that produced quick wins was increasing the target window on affected nodes and disabling sticky routing for the route. That points to routing + slot fragmentation as critical contributors.
- Prefill invalidations likely amplify the effect, increasing CPU pressure and making the window timers fire before good occupancy is reached.

Next experiments to run (ordered):
- Run a controlled A/B with three conditions for `chat-small` route for 1 hour: (A) sticky-routing on + default window, (B) sticky-routing off + default window, (C) sticky-routing on + window=15ms. Capture occupancy histograms and token throughput per-GPU. (Owner: Riley)
- Add a transient metric to batcher: percent of windows closed because of timer vs full occupancy. Add debug trace id to correlate with `route_hint` and `sticky` header. Short-term metric window: 3 hours. (Owner: Samir)
- Reproduce autoscaler rebalance locally in scale-test cluster and instrument active_slots change path. Try to force compaction to see impact on batch sizes. (Owner: Ava)
- Triage KV-prefill mismatch logs (trace a few requests end-to-end) to see whether prefill CPU spikes align with small-batch windows. (Owner: Samir)

Ops and safety notes:
- Avoid global rollback of cbatch-v2; that will impact latency on other workloads. Prefer canary experiments.
- If throughput continues to degrade and client impact > 25% for > 6h, escalate to on-call SRE and toggle `sticky-routing` feature flag as emergency mitigation. Document change in incident ticket (INF-2437).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did autoscaler rebalance trigger on 2024-11-01? Was it correlated with a cloud provider maintenance event? (check cloud provider health & event logs)
- Which clients are sending the `x-traffic-split=canary` header? Is there a new SDK that sets sticky hints incorrectly?
- Is there any clock skew between nodes causing timers to close early? Logs show up to 7ms skew on some messages; need to verify NTP/chrony.

Scratch CLI snippets to reproduce locally (dev cluster):
- start traffic generator: `python tools/traffic_gen.py --rate 1200rps --seq 64 --route chat-small --sticky-prob 0.3`
- enable detailed batcher debug: `rictl batcher set-log-level debug --node test-1`
- tail occupancy: `curl http://test-1:17000/debug/batcher/occupancy | jq .histogram`

Notes-to-self: capture a sample of 200 closed-window traces (ids) where occupancy <=3 and correlate with `route_hint` header + `active_slots` value in same second. That will help prove H1.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Launch A/B (Riley)
- [ ] Add metric for timer-closed vs full-closed windows (Samir)
- [ ] Run autoscaler compaction repro (Ava)
- [ ] Trace 50 KV-prefill mismatches end-to-end (Samir)
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton (after resolution)

If I forget: primary mitigations that helped in lab: increasing target window and disabling sticky-routing. Keep that as quick rollback path in incident.

-- Ava
